resources.string: Development only. Seeding saves opening accounting entries, not the complete game.
Earn %1$s net profit in a closed month
✓ Earned %1$s net profit in a closed month
Start with the menu and keep ingredients in stock. Watch what each sale earns and set aside money for bills. Your first milestone is to close a profitable month.
Use the shift and the overview to spot lost sales. If stock is the bottleneck, buy ingredients. If the team is overloaded, check Staff. Use Pause before making decisions.
Compare sales volume and profit before and after a price change. A discount can bring new groups. Make sure there is enough stock to serve them.
Choose how much stock to order and when to pay. Credit preserves cash today and creates a bill for later. Check shelf life before buying in bulk.
Compare purchases, consumption, waste and closing stock. Open an ingredient to see movements by day. Reduce orders if stock repeatedly expires.
Hire when groups are being lost to service capacity. Compare the extra wages with what those sales would earn. Staffing changes take effect the next day.
Check when the bank may run short. If there is money in the till, deposit it before a payment falls due. Forecast amounts depend on recent trading.
Review due dates and choose which bills to pay now. Late rent, wages and supplier bills can disrupt trading. Deposits move cash from the till to the bank.
Compare sales and expenses, then look at customer activity to explain the change. Profit includes accrued expenses such as wages and interest.
Check what the café owns, owes and has accumulated. Watch how inventory and unpaid bills change between reporting dates.
See where cash came from and where it went. Paying an old supplier invoice affects cash on the payment date. A transfer between till and bank leaves total cash unchanged.
Open a transaction to see its accounts and amounts. Use the journal to trace a report figure back to its transaction.
